en: The existence of Jesus was therefore separation from the world and flight from it into heaven; restoration of the life that comes away empty, in ideality; at every thing that conflicted with him, remembrance and looking up to God; but in part activity of the divine and to that extent struggle with fate, partly in spreading the kingdom of God, with the presentation of which the whole kingdom of the world collapsed and vanished in itself; partly in immediate reaction against individual parts of fate, just as they happened to strike against him, — except against the part of fate that appeared immediately as the state and also came to consciousness in Jesus, toward which he behaved passively.
zh: 所以，耶稣的存在就是与世界的分离，是从世界逃到天上；是把空手而去的生命在观念性中恢复过来；面对每一个与他相争的东西，就回忆并仰望上帝；但一部分是对神性的施行，就此而言是与命运的争战——这一方面是在传播上帝之国，随着对这国的展示，整个世界的王国就在自身中崩塌、消失了；另一方面是对命运各个部分的直接反应，只要它们恰好撞到他身上——唯独对命运中直接作为国家出现、并且在耶稣身上也进入意识的那一部分例外，对之他采取的是被动的态度。

en: The fate of Jesus was not entirely the fate of his congregation, since it was something composed out of several, who indeed lived in the same separation from the world, but each member found several like-minded people, they held together and could keep themselves more distant from the world in actuality, and since thereby there was less of meeting and of striking against it, they were less provoked by it, lived less in the negative activity of struggle, and the need for positive life had to become greater in them, for commonness of the negative gives no enjoyment, is no beauty.
Sublation of property, introduced community of goods, common meals belong more to the negative of union than that it would be a positive union.

The essence of their covenant was setting apart from human beings and love among one another; the two are necessarily connected; this love was not to be and could not be a union of individualities, but the union in God, and in God alone; in faith only that can unite itself which sets an actuality over against itself, sets itself apart from it; thereby this opposition was fixed and became an essential part of the principle of the covenant; and love had to keep always the form of love, of faith in God, without becoming living and presenting itself in shapes of life, because every shape of life can be grasped by the understanding as capable of being set over against it, as its object, as an actuality; and the relation to the world had to become an anxiousness before its touches, a fear of every form of life, because in each, since it has shape and is only one side, its lack can be shown, and this lacking thing is a share in the world.
Thus the covenant of the congregation found no reconciliation of fate, but the opposite extreme of the Jewish spirit, not the middle of the extremes in beauty.

The Jewish spirit had fixed the modifications of nature, the relations of life, into actualities, but as gifts of the ruler he was not only not ashamed of their poverty, but rather his pride and his life was the possession of actualities.

The spirit of the Christian congregation likewise saw actualities in every relation of life as it develops and presents itself; but since, as the feeling of love, objectivity was the greatest enemy to it, it remained just as poor as the Jewish spirit, but it despised the wealth for whose sake the Jewish spirit served.
zh: 耶稣的命运并不完全是他的教团的命运，因为教团是由多个人组合成的东西，这些人虽然生活在与世界同样的分离之中，但每个成员都找得到几个与他同调的人，他们聚在一起，在现实性中也能与尘世保持更远的距离；而既然这样，与世界的相遇和碰撞就少了，他们被它刺激得也就少了，更少生活在斗争的否定性活动里，于是对肯定性生命的需要在他们身上必然变得更大，因为否定之物的共同性不给人享受，也不是美。
扬弃财产、实行财产公有、共同进餐，这些更多属于结合的否定面，而不是一种肯定的结合。

他们的盟约的本质，就是从人群中分离出来，以及彼此之间的爱；这两者必然相连；这种爱不应当是、也不可能是诸个体性的结合，而是在上帝之中的结合，而且只在上帝之中；在信仰里，能够结合起来的只有那种把一种现实性设定在自己对面、并从其中分离出来的东西；这样一来，这种对立就被固定下来，成了盟约原则的一个本质部分；而爱必须始终保持着爱的形式、对上帝的信仰的形式，不能成为活的，不能在生命的诸形态中把自己展示出来，因为每一种生命形态都可能被知性当作可以置于对面的东西、当作它的对象、当作一种现实性来把握；与世界的关联也必然变成对它每一次触碰的担惊受怕，变成对任何一种生命形式的恐惧，因为在每一种形态里——既然它有形态，而且只是一个侧面——都能显出它的欠缺，而这欠缺的东西就是对世界的一份参与。
所以，教团的盟约没有找到命运的和解，而是找到了犹太精神那相反的一端，不是诸极端在美之中的中项。
犹太精神把自然的诸变化、生命的诸关系都固定成了现实性，但作为统治者的赠礼，他非但不为它们的贫乏感到羞耻，反而他的骄傲和他的生命就在于占有这些现实性。
基督教教团的精神同样在生命发展和展示自己的每一重关系里看到现实性；但既然对它来说，作为爱的感受，客观性是最大的敌人，它就仍然和犹太精神一样贫乏，只不过它鄙弃那种财富，而犹太精神正是为了这财富才服役的。

en: Life-despising enthusiasm can very easily pass over into fanaticism; for in order to preserve itself in its relationlessness, it must destroy that by which it is destroyed and which, even if it is the purest, is impure for it, must injure its content, often the most beautiful relations.

Enthusiasts of later times have made the despising of all forms of life, because they are polluted, into an unconditional empty shapelessness and have declared war on every drive of nature merely because it seeks an outer form, and the more terrible was the effect of these attempted suicides, of this holding fast to the empty unity, the firmer the bond of manifoldness still was in their minds; for since there was in them only the consciousness of limited forms, nothing remained to them but a flight into the void brought about by atrocities and devastations — but when the fate of the world became too great and maintained itself alongside and within the church, which is incompatible with it, there was no longer any thought of flight.

Great hypocrites against nature have therefore attempted to find and to maintain an unnatural connection of the manifoldness of the world and of the lifeless unity, of all limited lawful relations and human virtues, with the simple spirit; they devised for every civil action or for every expression of pleasure and desire a hiding corner in the unity, in order thus through deception at once to preserve every limitation for themselves, to enjoy it, and at the same time to escape it.
zh: 蔑视生命的狂热很容易转为偏执；因为要在自己的毫无关联中维持自己，它就必须毁掉那个毁掉它的东西——那东西即便最纯净，对它来说也是不纯净的——必须伤害它的内容，往往还伤害最美好的那些关系。

后世那些狂热者把对一切生命形式的鄙弃——因为它们被玷污了——弄成了一种无条件的、空洞的无形态状态，并向自然的每一种冲动宣战，只因为它在寻求一种外在形式；而人心里的杂多之束缚还越牢固，这些尝试性的自杀、这种死守空洞统一的举动的后果就越可怕；因为在他们心里只有对受限制形式的意识，所以留给他们的就只剩下一条靠暴行和毁灭来完成的逃进空无的路——但当世界的命运变得太大，并且在教会旁边、在教会内部把自己维持下来——教会与它是不能相容的——这时就再也谈不上逃走了。
所以，那些对自然大行伪善的人就试图找到并维持一种反自然的联结，把世界的杂多和无生命的统一、把一切受限制的法律性关系和人的美德，同单纯的精神联结起来；他们为每一种市民行为，或者为每一次快乐和欲望的流露，都在统一里想出一个藏身的角落，好靠欺骗既把每一种限制为自己保留下来，又享受它，同时又躲开它。

en: Since Jesus disdained to live with the Jews, but at the same time always fought against their actualities with his ideal, it could not fail that he had to succumb among them; he did not avoid this development of his fate, but he certainly did not seek it out either; to every enthusiast who enthuses only for himself, death is welcome, but whoever enthuses for a great plan can leave the scene on which he was to develop only with pain; Jesus died with the confidence that his plan would not be lost.
zh: 既然耶稣不屑于和犹太人一起生活，却又始终以自己的理想去对抗他们的种种现实性，那就免不了，他必定要在他们中间倒下；他并没有回避自己命运的这一发展，但他当然也没有去寻求它；对每一个只为自己而狂热的狂热者来说，死是受欢迎的，可是为一个宏大计划而狂热的人，只能带着痛苦离开那个本该让他展开自己的舞台；耶稣死时怀着这样的确信：他的计划不会落空。

en: Over against the negative side of the fate of the Christian congregation, the opposition to the world that turns the modifications of life into determinacies and the relations with them therefore into crimes, stands the positive side, the bond of love.

Through the extension of love to a whole congregation there enters into its character that it is not a living union of individualities, but that its enjoyment is restricted to the mutual consciousness that they love one another — the fatednesslessness through flight into unfulfilled life was made easier for the members of the congregation by the fact that they formed a congregation that refrained from all forms of life in relation to one another, or determined them only through the general spirit of love, that is, did not live in these forms — this love is a divine spirit, but not yet religion; for it to become that, it had to present itself at the same time in an objective form; it, a feeling, a subjective thing, had to melt together with what is represented, the universal, and thereby gain the form of a being capable of being worshipped and worthy of worship.

This need, to unite the subjective and the objective, the feeling and its demand for objects, the understanding, through the imagination, in a beautiful thing, a god, this need, the highest of the human spirit, is the drive toward religion.

For this drive of the Christian congregation, faith in God could not be satisfaction; for in their god only their common feeling had to find itself; in the god of the world all beings are united; the members of the congregation are not so as such in him; their harmony is not the harmony of the whole, otherwise they would not form a particular congregation, otherwise they would not be bound to one another by love; the divinity of the world is not the presentation of their love, of their divine element.

Jesus's need for religion was satisfied in the god of the whole; for his looking up to him was each of his constant collisions with the world, his flight from it; he needed only the opposite of the world, in which his opposition itself was grounded; he was his father, he was one with him.

But with his congregation the constant collision with the world fell away more, it lived without active struggle against it and was to that extent happy not to be constantly provoked by it and therefore not to have to flee only to the opposite, to God; rather it found in its community, in its love an enjoyment, something real, a kind of living relation; but since every relation is opposed to that which is related, and the feeling still has actuality, or, expressed subjectively, the capacity for it, the understanding, as something opposed to it, its lack had to be supplemented in something that unites both.

The congregation has the need of a god who is the god of the congregation, in which precisely the exclusive love, its character, its relation to one another is presented; not as a symbol or allegory, not as a personification of something subjective, in which one would be conscious of its separation from its presented [shape], but which is at the same time in the heart, at the same time feeling and object; feeling as spirit that breathes through all and remains one being, even if each individual becomes conscious of his feeling as his individual one.
zh: 基督教教团命运的否定面，即那种把生命的诸变化弄成种种规定性、从而把与它们的关系弄成罪行的对世界的对立，与之相对的是肯定面，即爱的纽带。

由于爱扩展到了整个教团，它的性格里就带上了这样一点：它不是诸个体性的活的结合，而是它的享受只限于彼此意识到自己在相爱——通过逃进未实现的生命而达到的无命运性，对教团成员来说之所以比较容易，是因为他们构成了一个教团，这个教团在彼此之间对一切生命形式都有所节制，或者只通过爱的普遍精神来规定它们，也就是说，并不生活在这些形式里——这种爱是一种神性的精神，但还不是宗教；要成为宗教，它就必须同时以一种客观的形式把自己展示出来；它作为一种感受、一种主观的东西，必须与那被表象的东西、与普遍的东西融汇在一起，从而获得一个可被崇拜、配得上崇拜的本质的形式。
这种需要，即把主观的东西和客观的东西、把感受以及感受对对象的要求、把知性，通过想象力在一个美的东西、一个神之中结合起来，这种需要，人的精神的最高需要，就是趋向宗教的冲动。
对基督教教团的这种冲动来说，对上帝的信仰不可能成为满足；因为在他们那个上帝里面，必定只能找到他们共同的感受；而世界的上帝里面，万物是结合着的；教团成员作为教团成员并不结合在他里面；他们的和谐不是整体的和谐，否则他们就不构成一个特殊的教团，否则他们就不会通过爱彼此结合；世界的神性并不是他们的爱、他们的神性的展示。
耶稣对宗教的需要，在整体的上帝里面得到了满足；因为他对上帝的仰望，就是他与世界的每一次不断碰撞，就是他对世界的逃离；他所需要的只是那与世界相对立的东西，而他的对立本身正是建立在这东西之中；上帝是他的父亲，他与上帝是一体的。

但在他的教团那里，与世界不断的碰撞就在更大程度上消失了，它活着而没有对世界展开行动上的斗争，就此而言它是幸运的：不必不断受它刺激，因此也不必只逃向那对立的东西、逃向上帝；相反，它在自己的共同体中、在自己的爱里找到了一种享受，一种真实的东西，一种活的关联；只是，既然每一种关系都与被关系者相对立，感受也还有现实性，或者用主观的方式说，还有感受的能力即知性作为与它相对立的东西，所以它的欠缺必须在一种把两者结合起来的东西里得到补足。
教团需要的是一个上帝，这个上帝是教团的上帝，在这个上帝里面，恰恰是那种排他的爱、它的性格、他们彼此的关系得到了展示；不是作为一个象征或寓言，不是作为一种主观之物的拟人化——在那种拟人化那里，人会意识到它与它所展示的[形态]的分离——而是一个同时就在心里、同时既是感受又是对象的东西；这感受作为精神，贯穿所有人，并且始终是一个本质，即便每一个个别的人都意识到自己的感受是他个别的感受。

en: A circle of love, a circle of minds that give up their rights to everything particular in relation to one another and are united only through common faith and hope, whose enjoyment and joy is solely this pure concord of love, is a small kingdom of God; but their love is not religion, for the unity, the love of human beings, does not at the same time contain the presentation of this unity.
Love unites them, but the beloved do not recognize this union; where they do recognize, they recognize something separated.

For the divine to appear, the invisible spirit must be united with something visible, so that everything is in one, cognition and feeling, so that there is a complete synthesis, a perfected harmony, so that harmony and the harmonious are one.

Otherwise there remains, in relation to the whole of separable nature, a drive that is too small for the infinity of the world and too great for its objectivity and cannot be satiated; there remains the inextinguishable, unsatisfied drive toward God.
zh: 一个爱的圈子，一个由这样一些心组成的圈子：他们在彼此之间放弃对一切特殊之物的权利，只通过共同的信仰和希望结合在一起，他们的享受和快乐就只是爱这种纯粹的一致，——这样一个圈子就是一个小小的上帝之国；但他们的爱还不是宗教，因为这种一致，人的爱，并不同时包含对这种一致的展示。
爱把他们结合起来，但被爱的人们并不认识这种结合；他们有所认识的地方，认识到的都是分离出来的东西。
要使神性的东西显现出来，不可见的精神就必须与可见的东西结合起来，使一切都在一个之中，认识与感受都在一个之中，使有一种完全的综合、一种完成了的和谐，使和谐与和谐的东西是一个。
否则，在可分离的自然这个整体面前，就还留着一种冲动，它对世界的无限性来说太小，对世界的客观性来说又太大，并且无法被喂饱；那不可磨灭的、得不到满足的趋向上帝的冲动就还留在那里。

en: After the death of Jesus his disciples were like sheep that have no shepherd; a friend had died on them, but they had also hoped that he was the one who would free Israel (Luk.

24, 21), and this hope was gone with his death; he had taken everything with him into the grave; his spirit had not remained in them.125) — Their religion, their faith in pure life, had hung on the individual, Jesus; he was their living bond and the revealed, shaped divine, in him God had also appeared to them, his individual united for them the indeterminate of harmony and the determinate in one living being.
With his death they were thrown back into the separation of the visible and the invisible, of the spirit and the actual.

True, the remembrance of this divine being, but now far from them, would have remained to them; the violence that his dying exercised over them would in time have been broken in them, the dead man would not have remained a mere dead man to them, the pain over the moldering body would gradually have yielded to the contemplation of his divinity; and the incorruptible spirit and the image of a purer humanity would have come forth for them out of his grave; but alongside the veneration of this spirit, the enjoyment of contemplating this image, the remembrance of the life of this image would have stood, this sublime spirit would always have had its opposite in his vanished existence; and its presence before the imagination would have been bound up with a longing that would only have designated the need of religion, but the congregation would still have had no god of its own.
zh: 耶稣死后，他的门徒就像没有牧人的羊；他们死了一个朋友，可是他们本来还希望，他就是那位要解放以色列的人（Luk.
24, 21），而这个希望随着他的死也破灭了；他把一切都带进了坟墓；他的精神没有留在他们里面。125）——他们的宗教、他们对纯净生命的信仰，本来一直系在耶稣这个个体身上；他是他们活的纽带，是那被启示出来的、有形态的神性，在他们看来，上帝也在他里面显现过，他的个体把和谐的未规定者和规定者在一个活的东西里为他们结合了起来。
随着他的死，他们又被抛回了可见者与不可见者、精神与现实者的分离之中。

诚然，对这一个神性本质的怀念会留给他们，不过这怀念现在离他们很远了；他的死对他们所施加的暴力，本来会随着时间在他们身上被折断，死者对他们本来不会一直只是一个死者，对那正在腐烂的肉体的痛苦本来会渐渐让位于对他神性的直观；而那不会腐朽的精神和更纯净的人性的形象，本来会从坟墓里向他们走出来；但是，在对这一精神的敬拜、在对这一形象的直观的享受旁边，本来还会立着对这一形象的生命的怀念，这个崇高的精神本来会始终在它那已经消逝的存在上拥有自己的对立面；而它出现在想象力面前，本来会与一种渴望相连，这渴望所标示的本来只是宗教的需要，可是教团本来还是没有一个属于自己的上帝。
